questions.q: Which of these is a valid, real constraint on an Azure Storage Account's `name` attribute?
options: It must be globally unique across all of Azure, using only lowercase letters and numbers, 3-24 characters long
It must contain at least one uppercase letter
It must be unique only within your own subscription, not across Azure
It may include hyphens and underscores freely
questions.explain: Storage account names share one global namespace across all Azure customers and are restricted to lowercase letters and digits.

options: How many copies of the storage account's data Azure keeps, and where (e.g. LRS, ZRS, GRS, RAGRS)
The programming language used to access the storage account
Whether the storage account is publicly accessible
The Terraform provider version used to create it
questions.explain: Replication type values like LRS (local) and GRS (geo-redundant) determine data redundancy and disaster-recovery posture.

questions.q: In the example configuration, why is the storage account's `name` built from a variable (`"ltvdataeng${var.environment}001"`) instead of a fixed string?
options: So the name stays valid and distinct per environment (dev, staging, prod) without hardcoding a new literal name each time
Because Terraform requires all resource names to reference a variable
Because fixed strings are not allowed in azurerm_storage_account blocks
It has no effect -- variables and fixed strings behave identically here
questions.explain: Building the name from a variable lets the same configuration produce a correctly named, non-colliding account per environment.

questions.q: What does `terraform plan` show before you run `terraform apply` on this configuration?
options: That 2 resources (the resource group and storage account) will be added, with 0 to change and 0 to destroy
The final bill for the resources about to be created
A live video feed of the Azure Portal
Nothing -- terraform plan does not report resource counts
questions.explain: terraform plan previews the exact actions apply would take, summarized as a count of resources to add, change, and destroy.
